//: Permission policy for the unattended Claude Code run in security-scan.yml ONLY — passed explicitly via `claude --settings .github/security-scan-permissions.json`, deliberately NOT named .claude/settings.json, which Claude Code auto-discovers for every session in this repo (an earlier version of this file lived there and briefly locked an interactive session out of .github/** and .claude/** before being moved here). There is no human to answer a permission prompt in the unattended run, so this scopes exactly what can run without one, command-by-command (not whole-binary wildcards) — anything not explicitly listed is denied outright rather than bypassed. Edit/Write on .github/** and .claude/** itself are explicitly denied so the automation can never loosen its own guardrails or rewrite the deploy pipeline. The repo owner separately confirmed allowing `gh workflow run ci-cd.yml --ref main` specifically, since that triggers an unattended production deploy.
